content.text:
I checked 17 claims and flagged none. Each one traces to a line in the record:
- **What the change did:** the deploy diff (D1) shows the line that kept the monthly total updated was removed.
- **What still reads that total:** the code rows U1–U6 show the statement, the spend summary and the reconciliation check all still read the stored figure.
- **The running code:** the source at the deployed revision (S1) shows neither way of recording a purchase updates the monthly total.
- **Timing and scope:** the deploy times (P1, P2), the rollout read (T11) and the alert (AL1) support the timeline and the ruled-out earlier deploy.

Two calls were close, and I accepted both:
- **"Every purchase recorded afterwards left the stored figure further behind" (root cause).** Strictly, only purchases in the current month push the total further behind. The record backs the substance, though, and a wrong flag costs as much as a missed one.
- **"Each affected total came out short" (causal chain 1).** The alert only gives the widest gap as a shortfall. But the running code never raises the monthly total, so every affected total can only fall short.

I didn't judge the action items or the "had it been otherwise" sentences, as instructed.

supported.quote: The change removed the line in record_purchase that added each in-month purchase's price to the account's stored total_this_month_cents, on the reasoning that the month could be derived from the purchase history, yet left the stored field in place.

The monthly statement still reads that field as the month total and divides it by the number of purchases to get the mean, the spend summary divides it by the number of this month's purchases, and the reconciliation check compares it with the sum of this month's purchase prices.
So every purchase recorded afterwards left the stored figure further behind the purchases.

A code change to the shop stopped updating each shopper's saved running total for the current month when a purchase was recorded, but the shop's statements and checks still read that saved total, so it fell further behind what shoppers had actually bought.

Every purchase recorded through either write path on the running revision could keep leaving shoppers' stored monthly totals short, and the totals already written wrong stay wrong in the monthly statements and spend figures that read them until someone rewrites them.
Shoppers' monthly spend totals fell short of the purchases behind them
Shoppers' stored monthly spend totals no longer matched the purchases behind them: each affected total came out short of what the shopper had bought this month.

Purchases recorded on the running code were added to the account and to the lifetime total, but the stored this-month total was left where it was. The reconciliation check compares that stored figure with the sum of the in-month purchases, so it found the stored figure short.
Revision 26f1d7e, deployed at {P2.1}, removed the update to total_this_month_cents from record_purchase. As of {T11.1}, all {T11.2} replicas were running that revision.
The earlier deploy of revision 4c810f2 at {P1.1}: the alert dates the oldest affected purchase at {A4}, which is after the later deploy at {P2.1}.

The change stopped keeping the month total on the reasoning that it could be derived from the history, but it left the stored field in place, and the monthly statement, the spend summary and the reconciliation check all still read that stored field.
The only thing that found the drift was the spend-integrity check, which runs once every {A5} days.
No more frequent check was seen comparing stored monthly totals with the purchases behind them.
Before the change was deployed, no check was seen that records purchases through the ledger's write paths and confirms the stored monthly total still matches the purchases.
The alert paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it, so the rollback Argus recommended waited on a person noticing it.
